title: Access governance on-call runbook: RBAC v2, audit queries, and SSO/SAML troubleshooting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Provide a concise, operational runbook for on-call engineers and support to handle RBAC v2 incidents, audit-log investigations, and SSO/SAML user access failures. This document complements the longer admin guide (Confluence) and the RBAC design doc in the repo. Scope: - Emergency access escalation and just-in-time (JIT) workflows for RBAC v2 - Common audit log queries for account activity, privilege changes, and policy evaluation results - SSO/SAML troubleshooting checklist (IdP metadata, cert rotation, mappings) - Support macros for ticket responses and quick remediation steps - Rollback and verification steps after role/policy changes Related artifacts: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Design - Admin guide: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Admin+Guide - GitHub PR (policy engine): https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-engine/pull/3456 - Audit dashboard (Kibana): https://dash.redwood.com/app/kibana#/dashboard/rbac-audit-logs

Runbook excerpts (actionable steps):
1) Initial triage: determine impact and scope
   - Verify reporter identity and reproduction steps.
   - Check service health: redwoodctl status (example):
     redwoodctl status --component policy-engine --env prod
   - Identify affected users/resources from ticket notes.

2) Quick containment for unauthorized access
   - If a user reports access they shouldn't have, immediately enumerate active sessions and tokens: 
     API call to sessions endpoint (internal): curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood.com/v1/sessions?user_email=alice@example.com
   - Revoke tokens and active sessions: redwoodctl sessions revoke --user alice@example.com --reason "emergency revoke"
   - Temporarily apply a deny-all override to the affected policy path:
     redwoodctl policy override apply --path "/orgs/1234/*" --effect deny --ttl 30m --note "investigation"
   - Notify stakeholders (incident channel) with the support macro (below).

3) Investigating RBAC changes in audit logs
   - Key audit events: ROLE_ASSIGNMENT, POLICY_PATCH, POLICY_OVERRIDE, SSO_ASSERTION_FAILURE, TOKEN_REVOKE
   - Example Kibana query to find role grants in the last 24h:
     event.type:ROLE_ASSIGNMENT AND event.outcome:success AND @timestamp:[now-24h TO now]
   - Example SQL (elastic) for policy edits:
     SELECT timestamp, actor, change_summary FROM audit_events WHERE event_type='POLICY_PATCH' AND timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days' ORDER BY timestamp DESC;
   - Look for correlated SSO events (IdP assertions) within a ±5 minute window of suspicious policy edits.

4) SSO/SAML troubleshooting checklist
   - Symptoms: users cannot sign in, attribute mapping incorrect, intermittent failures.
   - Quick checks:
     - Confirm IdP metadata is up-to-date: Admin Console -> Auth -> SAML -> Identity Provider Metadata URL.
     - Verify certificate expiry: check idp x509 cert thumbprint against IdP.
     - Check clock skew: ensure IdP and Redwood servers within 2 minutes.
     - Inspect SAML assertion in logs (redacted): search for SSO_ASSERTION_FAILURE with details.
     - Validate attribute mappings: ensure 'email' and 'groups' attributes map to expected fields in RBAC v2.
     - If SAML logout issues: confirm SP-initiated logout URL and binding match IdP config.
   - Recovery steps:
     - If metadata changed recently, re-publish new metadata and rotate the SP certificate during low-traffic window.
     - For attribute mapping regressions, use temporary group-to-role mapping in RBAC console and record TTL for removals.

5) Just-in-time (JIT) temporary access pattern
   - Use ephemeral role grants for approved on-call actions:
     - Request approval via PagerDuty/Slack escalation with approver tag(s).
     - Apply grant: redwoodctl rbac grant --user bob@example.com --role support_oncall --ttl 1h --reason "investigation"
     - Log approval in ticket and add audit comment: ticket.comment "JIT granted by @sam (approved)"
   - Post-action: confirm logs show ROLE_ASSIGNMENT and ROLE_REVOKE events. Add remediation checklist to ticket.

6) Rollback and verification after policy change
   - If a policy change caused regressions, rollback using the policy engine's version history:
     redwoodctl policy rollback --policy-id pol_0x73 --to-version 67 --reason "rollback after regression"
   - Verify access matrix for a sample of users: redwoodctl rbac check --user test@redwood.com --resource /orgs/1234 --actions read,write
   - Run automated smoke checks (internal suite) and validate audit events for the rollback.

Support macros (copy-paste ready)
- Macro: emergency-revoke
  "We detected an access issue. We've revoked active sessions and applied a temporary deny override while we investigate. We'll follow up with timeline and remediation steps in this ticket. If you need immediate access, request JIT grant via the on-call channel." 
- Macro: sso-failed-assertion
  "We've observed SAML assertion errors for your organization. Ask your IdP admin to confirm metadata and certificate validity. We've captured the failing assertion ID: {{assertion_id}} and escalated to engineering if it persists." 
- Macro: role-granted-temp
  "Temporary access granted for investigation. This grant expires in {{ttl}}. Please confirm you can reproduce the issue and we'll revoke when complete." 

Escalation and contacts
- On-call security engineer: @sec-oncall (PagerDuty)
- Policy engine owner: liam.oconnor@redwood.com
- Auth platform lead: aisha.patel@redwood.com
- SSO vendor escalation (for IdP outages): okta-support@okta.com (follow vendor SLA)

Post-incident actions
- Create a post-mortem entry with timelines and root cause.
- If RBAC policies were changed as workarounds, schedule a follow-up to convert temporary fixes into safe, audited changes.
- Add failed assertions and related audit events as regression cases to the CI smoke suite.

Notes and links for deeper troubleshooting
- Policy engine logs (internal stackdriver): projects/redwood/logs/policy-engine
- Audit queries cookbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/Audit+Queries+Cookbook
- RBAC v2 semantics doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Semantics
